Acetaminophen is analgesic antipyretic used in treatment of mild to moderate pain and fever, it work by inhibiting the prostaglandin synthesis in the brain

Acetaminophen is well tolerated by most people

But some times it may lead to side effects which we will talk about here

Liver damage

Acetaminophen is metabolized in the liver and it can be toxic to the liver when taken In high doses

Even in normal doses there is risk for hepatotoxicity

Liver damage may manifest as acute liver failure

Symptoms include nausea, vomiting, loss of appetite, sweating, confusion, abdominal pain and yellowish discoloration of skin and eyes

blood disorders

Anemia, leukopenia, neutropenia, pancytopenia

Symptoms of these conditions include unusual bleeding or bruising, fatigue and increased susceptibility to infections

Electrolyte imbalances

Such as decreased serum bicarbonate, reduced concentrations of sodium and calcium, hyperammonemia, hyperchloremia, hyperuricemia , increase serum glucose and elevated levels of bilirubin and alkaline phosphatase

Hypersensitivity reactions (Allergic reactions)

Skin rash , itching, swelling of the face, tongue or throat, trouble breathing

toxic epidermal necrolysis, SJ syndrome

Other side effects

Abdominal pain

Nausea and vomiting

Increased risk for GIT bleeding

Increased risk for stroke and MI

Rarely may lead to drug induced lung injury

Rarely may lead to kidney impairment characterized by elevated urea and creatinine
